edgware.s1_head: Kitting the events trade of north-west London and Barnet
s1loc: Edgware sits at the top of Barnet, close to the borough's big-event clusters. StoneX Stadium at Mill Hill runs Saracens fixtures and concerts with shuttle buses from Edgware station, the RAF Museum London at Colindale hosts events and outdoor screenings, and Brent Cross Town is building a programme of seasonal markets and live days. Add the free Edgware Community Carnival and the production crews working out of Elstree Studios at nearby Borehamwood, and the local events calendar fills out across the year.

And the trade runs at every size. Major venues, stadiums, festival operators and production companies run big crews and large seasonal teams and buy through procurement, while independent event crews, promoters and entertainers around Edgware and the wider Barnet borough need just a few branded pieces. A workwear supplier here has to serve the big stadium event and the single crew alike, which is why we run trade accounts and direct online ordering side by side.

bury.s1_head: Kitting the events trade of Bury and the Manchester north
s1loc: Bury has a live scene that punches above its size. The Met on Market Street, in the Victorian Derby Hall, runs a busy programme of music, theatre and comedy and promotes the Head for the Hills festival, which fills Burrs Country Park each September. Bury Town Hall hosts civic events and shows, and the August bank holiday brings the Glaston-Bury weekend. Brightside Brewery in nearby Radcliffe pours at the festival, tying Whitefield and the wider borough into the events calendar.

Fort Amherst adds the Summer Proms at its Spur Battery amphitheatre, and Rochester and Strood next door keep the calendar busy through the season.

s1loc: Paisley has a deep events tradition. Paisley Town Hall stages live shows and runs the Paisley Book and Comedy festivals, while The Spree fills the town each October as one of Scotland's leading arts festivals, with gigs in Paisley Abbey and the Spiegeltent. The Bungalow on Shuttle Street is the grassroots room, where bands cut their teeth, and Sma' Shot Day, one of the world's oldest workers' festivals, parades from Brodie Park to Abbey Close each July with live music and street performance.

carlisle.s1_head: Kitting the events trade of Carlisle and the Cumbrian north
s1loc: Carlisle is the events hub for a wide stretch of Cumbria. The Sands Centre is the region's main entertainment and music venue, handling touring shows, comedy and pantomime, while open-air concerts at Bitts Park, beneath Carlisle Castle, have drawn names like Tom Jones and Jess Glynne. The riverside park also hosts the Fireshow each autumn for crowds of tens of thousands, and Taste Cumbria brings its food and live-music festival to the Cathedral grounds and the Greenmarket.

crewe.s1_head: Kitting the events trade of Crewe and south Cheshire
s1loc: Crewe's live scene centres on its Edwardian theatre. The Crewe Lyceum Theatre, a Grade II listed 677-seat house on Heath Street, runs musicals, drama, comedy and pantomime, with the smaller Lyceum Studio backing new writing and up-and-coming acts. Queens Park, the Victorian park gifted to the town by the railway in 1887, takes the open-air events, hosting free music days like Picnic in the Park and the Cheshire East Armed Forces Weekend, giving south Cheshire a steady summer calendar.

And the trade runs at every size.
